COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
 WPMS No.110 of 2025
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.

Mr. B.S. Koranga, Advocate for the

Mr. Yogesh Chandra Tiwari,
Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand.

2. Proceeding under Uttar Pradesh
Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised
Occupants) Act, 1972 were initiated
against the petitioner, which resulted in
passing of an eviction order dated
25.04.2024. Against the eviction order,
petitioner filed an Appeal under Section 9
of the said Act. His Appeal has been
dismissed on the ground of delay by
learned District Judge, Nainital vide
judgment dated 30.11.2024. Thus,
feeling aggrieved, petitioner has
approached this Court challenging the
judgment & order passed by learned
District Judge in Misc. Application No.131
of 2024.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that the delay condonation
application has been wrongly rejected,
Prescribed Authority proceeded ex parte
in the m atter due to petitioner's non
appearance on a certain date, and
petitioner was not aware about the order
passed by Prescribed Authority until
24.10.2024, when the Halka Patwari
informed him about passing of eviction
order against him . He submits that
appellant applied for certified copy of the
eviction order, which was delivered to
him on 28.10.2024 and soon thereafter

2025:UHC:466
he filed the appeal. Thus, he submits
that the prayer for delay condonation
m ade by petitioner deserved to be
allowed and learned Court below has
rejected the sam e by taking a hyper-technical view.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner
has referred to the application seeking
condonation of delay, which is on record
at page no. 41 of the writ petition. I n the
delay condonation application, petitioner
has pleaded that he had engaged a
counsel for appearing before the
Prescribed Authority, who had assured
him that he will sum mon the petitioner
as and when required by the Prescribed
Authority; due to COVI D-19 Pandemic,
petitioner lost track of the proceedings
pending before Prescribed Authority and
he also lost contact with his counsel and
he was under the im pression that his
counsel would be pursuing the m atter,
however, on 24.10.2024 the Patwari
informed him about passing of eviction
order, and petitioner then cam e to
Nainital on 26.10.2024 and applied for
certified copy of the eviction order, which
was delivered to him on 28.10.2024, and
after drafting the Appeal, the sam e is
filed in Court today. Thus, petitioner
prayed that benefit of Section 5
Limitation Act be given to him and the
Appeal be heard and decided on m erits.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner
refers to Section 9(2) of Uttar Pradesh
Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised
Occupants) Act, 1972. Proviso to Section
9(2) of the aforesaid Act enables the
Appellate Authority to entertain the
Appeal after expiry of the lim itation
period if he satisfied that the appellant
was prevented by sufficient cause from

2025:UHC:466
filing an appeal in tim e. For ready
reference Section 9 (2) of the Act is
extracted below: -
"9. Appeals.-(1).........
(2) An appeal under sub-section (1) shall be
preferred-
(a)in the case of an appeal from an order under
Section 5, within fifteen days from the date of
publication of the order under sub-section (1) of
that section; and
(b)in the case of an appeal from an order under
Section 7, within fifteen days from the date on
which the order is communicated to the appellant:
Provided that the Appellate Officer may entertain
the appeal after the expiry of the said period of
fifteen days, if he is satisfied that the appellant was
prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal
in time."
6. Learned Appellate Court has
rejected the delay condonation
application by holding that sufficient
cause has not been shown for the delay
caused in filing the appeal. From perusal
of the im pugned judgm ent, it is revealed
that the past conduct of the petitioner of
not pursuing the m atter diligently in the
proceedings before the Prescribed
Authority has been m ade the basis for
rejecting his prayer for delay
condonation. I n his application, petitioner
has indicated the reasons for his non
appearance before the Prescribed
Authority.
7. Even otherwise also, lack of
diligence on the part of petitioner in
pursuing the m atter before the
Prescribed Authority cannot be a good
ground for rejecting his prayer for
condonation of delay in filing the appeal.
The explanation for the delay offered by
the petitioner that he came to know
about eviction order only on 24.10.2024
and certified copy of the eviction order

2025:UHC:466
was delivered on 28.10.2024, appears to
be sufficient for condonation of delay.
8. Law is well settled that while
considering prayer for condonation of
delay, a liberal and justice oriented
approach has to be adopted. Since
Prescribed Authority has ordered for
petitioner's eviction from the land in
question, therefore, he would not get
any benefit out of the delay in filing the
appeal. Therefore, in the absence of
objection filed by the State, the cause
shown by the petitioner cannot be
disbelieved. Lack of diligence on the part
of the petitioner in pursuing the m atter
before the Prescribed Authority cannot
be a valid ground for rejecting his delay
condonation application.
9. I n such view of the m atter, the writ
petition is allowed; impugned judgment
dated 30.11.2024 passed by learned
District Judge is quashed and the delay
condonation application filed by the
petitioner stands allowed. The Appeal
filed by the petitioner shall stand
restored to the file of learned District
Judge, who shall decide the Appeal on
m erits.
 ( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
